title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0LC0RF_1RD0LB_1RE1RD_1RA0RC_1LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0LC0RF_1RD0LB_1RE1RD_1RA0RC_1LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of numbers in unary (blocks of 4k+3 ones) that each round trip rewrites; the sweep rules over the blocks are proved in Lean, but the rewriting of the list has no known closed form and looks chaotic. No halt in 1010 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right; F with 1 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: 10 rules for all values of the repeat counts and every tape around them: the leftward sweep turns each 11 of a block into 10 (B) or 01 (C), the rightward sweep turns 001, 010, 100 into 110, 101, 011 (C, D, E), the left end of a block, and the turns at the two ends.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,588 cells have been visited and 21,207 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun 1RB1LE_0LC0RF_1RD0LB_1RE1RD_1RA0RC_1LB--- 10000000000 runs 1010 steps without a halt (96,115 ones at the end).

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).

claims.title: Blocks of 4k+3 ones
claims.text: At every 7th visit to the right end in the first 3·108 steps, 553,908 of the 554,278 blocks of ones between single 0s have a length 4k+3; the few others are where the head was still working. After a leftward sweep a block of 4k+3 ones has become 2k+1 single 1s (000 (10)^(2k+1)), the groups separated by 000.

claims.title: The halting state is never close
claims.text: F1 is the only halting transition and F is entered only by B1 (0RF): a halt needs B on a 1 with a 1 after it. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps F is entered 117,032,159 times and reads 0 every time.

claims.title: The same table as 1RB1RA_1RC0RE
claims.text: Renaming A, B, C, D, E, F to C, D, E, A, B, F gives the table of 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---, so this machine is that one started in state C.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 7 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of numbers is rewritten each round trip by a sequential process with a finite carry (the zigzag of the rightward sweep), but how the list evolves is not understood; a proof would need an invariant of the list (a closed language of lists) that keeps B away from two adjacent 1s.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_1LB1RE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a list of numbers written in unary, each a block of 4k+3 ones; every round trip of the head rewrites the list. This page shows the encoding, the proved sweep rules, and what a halt would need.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
The sweep rules of lean/Rules.lean, for every repeat count.

sections.heading: A list of unary numbers, rewritten every round trip
sections.html:
The head runs from end to end; a visit adds 1 to 4 cells at the left end and 3 to 8 at the right. Just after a rightward sweep the tape is a list of blocks of ones separated by single 0s, and almost every block has a length 4k+3: the tape is a list of numbers k1, k2, ... in unary. The leftward sweep rewrites each block: state B turns each pair 11 into 10, and the left end of a block 0111 into 00010, so a block of 4k+3 ones becomes 2k+1 single 1s, 000 1 0 1 0 ... 1 0, and the blocks are separated by 000. The rightward sweep zigzags: at every block it backs up a few cells, and over the inside of a block it turns 001, 010, 100 into 110, 101, 011 (states C, D, E), rebuilding blocks of 4k+3 ones, but not the same ones.

How the list changes from one round trip to the next has no known formula. Seen at the right end, the first numbers repeat a short cycle (1 0 0 3 1 0 0 ... comes back every few round trips) while the rest looks random: the run is a one-dimensional cellular automaton on the list, seen once per round trip.

sections.html:
Each row is a theorem of lean/Rules.lean, for every n and every tape L, R (S>: the head in state S on the next cell; (w)^n: n copies of w; 0^inf: blank tape).

sections.heading: What a halt would need
sections.html:
F1 is the only halting transition, and F is entered only from B on a 1 (writing 0, moving right). So the machine halts exactly when B reads a 1 followed by another 1. In the first 109 steps F is entered 117,032,159 times; the cell after was 0 every time. No halt in 1010 steps.

Twin of 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- (1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---): renaming the states A, B, C, D, E, F here to C, D, E, A, B, F gives that machine's table, so this one is it started in its state C (without the two 1s that machine writes first). The runs differ cell by cell but have the same structure.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,588 cells (6,817 left of the start, 20,161 right), with a density of 1s of 0.58.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_1LB1RE: rename A→F, B→B, C→C, D→D, E→E, F→A and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state F, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F; it is this table started in state D

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LE_1RC0RE_1RD0RA_1RE1LC_0LA0RF_1LE---: 9,589,851 configurations, the last at step 9,589,854 here and step 10,000,000 there

summary: A bouncer whose tape, after a rightward sweep, is a list of numbers k written as blocks of 4k+3 ones separated by single 0s; each round trip rewrites the list in a cellular-automaton-like way; halting needs B on two adjacent 1s, never seen.
family: bouncer over a list of unary numbers
